intended_use: Research screening support on anonymized/test data. Not a diagnosis; not validated for clinical use.

pipeline.pooling: max over all time frames (no chunking)
pipeline.standardization: StandardScaler fit on the training split only (scaler.npz)
pipeline.head: Linear(1024,128) - ReLU - Dropout(0.3, train only) - Linear(128,1); sigmoid = P(ALS)
pipeline.decision_rule: argmax over [1-p, p] (equivalent to p >= 0.5) for the reported test counts

data_split.dataset: SAND Challenge Task 1 training sheet; Class 5 = HC (0), Class 1-4 = ALS (1)
data_split.unit: subject (speaker) - no speaker appears in two splits

test.level: recording (328 recordings from 41 held-out subjects); not subject-level aggregation

limitations: history.csv has more epochs than the notebook's MAX_EPOCHS/PATIENCE allow, and validation.json differs from the notebook's printed value for this layer (72.09%). This indicates the supplied artifacts were not produced by the run whose output is saved in the notebook. The validation count (239/326) and test total (328) match the notebook's subject split, but no training run ID was saved, so the weights-to-run link is consistent, not proven.
test_confusion_counts.npy is taken to belong to head.pt because they were supplied together; re-running inference on the SAND test split is the only way to verify it.
Test metrics are internal (same SAND distribution, same recording protocol). They are not the performance of the deployed app on phone recordings, other microphones, or other populations.
Recordings are not independent: 8 recordings per subject on average, so recording-level metrics overstate the effective sample size.
Specificity is low relative to sensitivity at the 0.5 threshold; no clinical operating point was validated.
